SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - OCTOBER 7, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
OCTOBER 7, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Paul Hansen, First Christian Reformed Church of
  Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth Flag
  Football Team - Bills.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Scott Smith, ABCUSD Communications Director, provided updates regarding projects
  which are funded with Measure BB proceeds.

  Mel Cortez thanked the City Council for their hard work, suggested a partnership
  with the Chamber of Commerce as related to the community calendar, inquired
  regarding CCPA discounts for Cerritos residents, and encouraged the community to
  attend the upcoming Community Safety Town Hall at CPE on Wednesday, October
  16, 2019.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  September 26, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of September 26, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  October 7, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 7, 2019
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  10/07/2019  $4,670,808.80 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts 2019-
  2020 Calendar of Events, Bid No. 1386-19 (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar by Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama for
  separate consideration.

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to a contract for the
  printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts 2019-2020 Calendar of
  Events to Southwest Offset Printing in the amount of $51,284.75, Bid No. 1386-19.
  In the event issues of non-performance arise, the project would be removed from
  Southwest Offset Printing and taken to the next lowest bidder to ensure the City’s
  printing deadline, quality standards and specifications are met. This process would
  be repeated as necessary in order of the lowest bid to the highest (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 7, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  Award of an ongoing contract for traffic engineering services in the City of Cerritos,
  RFP No. 1382-19 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award an ongoing contract for traffic engineering services in the City of Cerritos
  to Hartzog & Crabill, Inc. for twelve (12) months with a provision for up to three
  (3) twelve-month extensions and under the additional terms as specified in the
  agreements, RFP No. 1382-19; and

  2. Award an ongoing contract for traffic engineering services in the City of Cerritos
  to Albert Grover & Associates for twelve (12) months with a provision for up to
  three (3) twelve-month extensions and under the terms as specified in the
  agreements, RFP No. 1382-19; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute said contractual agreements on behalf of
  the City of Cerritos, including any contract modifications that may be necessary
  to complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of an ongoing contract for civil engineering services in the City of Cerritos,
  RFP No. 1383-19 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract for civil engineering services in the City of Cerritos to Willdan
  Engineering for twelve (12) months with a provision for up to three (3) twelve-
  month extensions and under the terms as specified in the agreements, RFP No.
  1383-19; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute said agreement on behalf of the City of
  Cerritos, including any contract modifications that may be necessary to
  complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 7, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7F.  Award of a contract for sewer design services for the Ground Water Treatment
  Station at the Civic Center parking structure, RFP No. 1387-19 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract in an amount not to exceed $22,420 for sewer design
  services for the Ground Water Treatment Station at the Civic Center parking
  structure, RFP No. 1387-19, to Mullholland Consulting, Inc. and reject the other
  bid; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational report to the Cerritos City Council
  providing information related to the upcoming 2020 United States Census and the
  City of Cerritos’ proposed U.S. Census action plan (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Alfonso Manzo, representing the Office of Congresswoman Linda Sanchez, spoke
  regarding the Congresswoman's efforts related to 2020 Census projects.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to direct staff to implement
  the City of Cerritos’ U.S. Census Action Plan and to receive and file the report.

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 7, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration of playground equipment at El Rancho Verde Park,
  Sunshine Park and Westgate Park (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Parks
  and Recreation Commission’s recommendations for the selection of new playground
  equipment color palettes at the following City parks:

  1. “Deep Space” color palette for the new playground equipment at El Rancho Verde
  Park; and

  2. “Atlantic” color palette for the new playground equipment at Sunshine Park; and

  3. “Desert” color palette for the new playground equipment at Westgate Park
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an informational report on the City of Cerritos Coyote
  Management Plan (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Colleen Aldrich expressed support for education related to coyotes in the
  community.

  Garry Aldrich expressed support for additional education and enforcement related
  to coyotes in the community.

  Mel Cortez expressed support for education related to the coyotes in the
  community. He submitted a document for the record entitled, “Coyote sightings in
  Cerritos.”

  Mike Villani expressed support for augmented enforcement related to coyotes in
  the community.

  Cynthia Navarro noted the coyote problem in the community is increasing and
  expressed support for enforcement alternatives.

  Shebani Patel and Rupa Eadani expressed concerns coyote hazing methods may
  not be effective.
 City of Cerritos  October 7, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  Matthew Duncan did not support aggressive removal of coyotes from the local
  ecosystem.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to receive and file the
  report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Pulido, Mayor Pro
  Tem Yokoyama and Mayor Solanki.

12.  Closed Session

  12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Manager

  12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk/Treasurer

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT: The City Attorney reported the City Council met in
  Closed Session to discuss items 12A, 12B, and 12C as listed on the Closed Session
  agenda. The City Council discussed the items and there was no reportable action
  taken in Closed Session.
 City of Cerritos  October 7, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 7

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 10:55 p.m.
